questions.question: What is the purpose of User Keywords in Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To create reusable higher-level actions by combining existing keywords
To abstract complex sequences into named actions
To execute keywords faster than library keywords
options.explanation: User Keywords are for organization, not performance

questions.question: Where are User Keywords defined?

options.text: In the *** Keywords *** section of suite files or resource files

options.explanation: Test Cases is for tests, not keyword definitions
Variables section is for data, not keywords
Keywords are defined in *** Keywords *** section

questions.question: How is the *** Keywords *** section structured?

options.text: User keyword names are unindented; their bodies are indented by multiple spaces
All keyword definitions are indented consistently
options.explanation: Names are unindented; only bodies are indented

options.text: Keywords use curly braces to define their scope
options.explanation: RF uses indentation, not braces

options.text: Keywords must be separated by blank lines
options.explanation: Blank lines are optional for readability

questions.question: What is the difference in scope between User Keywords defined in suite files vs resource files?

options.text: Suite keywords are local to that suite; resource keywords can be used in any suite that imports the resource
There is no difference; both are globally available
options.explanation: Suite keywords have limited scope
Resource keywords are meant to be imported and shared
Performance is not affected by location

questions.question:
Analyze this User Keyword structure:

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Verify Valid Login
    [Arguments]    ${exp_full_name}
    ${version}=    Get Server Version
    Should Not Be Empty    ${version}
    ${name}=    Get User Name
    Should Be Equal    ${name}    ${exp_full_name}
```

What elements are present? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Indented keyword body with settings and keyword calls

options.explanation: This keyword doesn't have a [Return] or RETURN statement

questions.question: What characteristics should User Keyword names have?

options.text: Reflecting the purpose of the keyword

options.explanation: Case doesn't matter; names are case-insensitive

questions.question: How does Robot Framework match keyword names?

options.explanation: All special characters are normalized during matching

questions.question: Which of these keyword names are considered identical by Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Dots are not ignored; this would be different

questions.question: What is the keyword matching algorithm when an exact match is not found?

options.text: Try removing BDD prefixes (Given/When/Then/And/But), then try embedded argument matching
Immediately fail with keyword not found error
options.explanation: RF tries multiple matching strategies

options.text: Use the first keyword that partially matches
options.explanation: RF uses specific matching strategies, not partial matching

options.text: Ask the user which keyword to use
options.explanation: Matching is automatic using defined algorithms

questions.question: What is the default naming convention for Library Keywords?

options.text: Title Case with capital letters at the beginning of each word and spaces between words

options.explanation: Library keywords typically use Title Case
Library keywords typically use Title Case with spaces
Library keywords typically use Title Case

questions.question: What settings are available for User Keywords? (Select all that apply)
What is the purpose of the [Documentation] setting in User Keywords?

options.text: To provide a description of the keyword's purpose and usage

options.explanation: [Arguments] defines arguments, not [Documentation]
[Documentation] is for description, not execution control
RF doesn't have permission settings

questions.question: What part of keyword documentation appears in log.html as short documentation?

options.text: The first logical line until the first empty row

options.explanation: Only the first logical line is used as short documentation
The first line is used for short documentation
Short documentation comes from the first line of [Documentation]

questions.question: What documentation formatting does Robot Framework support? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: RF format is similar to but not compatible with Markdown

questions.question: What is the purpose of the [Arguments] setting?

options.text: To define the arguments a user keyword expects

options.explanation: [Documentation] is for documentation, not [Arguments]
[Arguments] is for inputs, not outputs
[Timeout] sets timeout, not [Arguments]

questions.question: How are arguments defined in User Keywords?

options.text: As scalar variables ${arg} separated by multiple spaces
In parentheses after the keyword name
options.explanation: RF uses [Arguments] setting, not parentheses
RF uses space separation, not commas

options.text: With type declarations like int, str
options.explanation: User Keywords cannot define argument types

questions.question: Can User Keywords define argument types (like string, number)?

options.text: No, User Keywords cannot define argument types
Yes, using type hints like ${arg: int}
options.explanation: Type hints are for Library Keywords, not User Keywords
No [Types] setting exists for User Keywords

options.text: Yes, but only for optional arguments
options.explanation: User Keywords don't support type definitions

questions.question: What makes an argument mandatory in a User Keyword?

options.text: Defined as ${arg} without a default value

options.explanation: No special tag needed; lack of default makes it mandatory
Case doesn't determine if argument is mandatory

options.text: All arguments are mandatory by default
options.explanation: Arguments with defaults are optional
Arguments without defaults are mandatory
Both arguments lack defaults, so both are mandatory
server_log is a local variable, not an argument

questions.question: What is the scope of variables defined in [Arguments]?

options.text: Local to the keyword body; they don't exist outside the keyword

options.explanation: Argument variables are local to the keyword
Arguments are locally scoped
Arguments must be passed explicitly to called keywords

questions.question: How do you define optional arguments in User Keywords?

options.text: By assigning default values using = without spaces: ${arg}=default

options.explanation: Use default values, not tags

options.text: By putting them in square brackets: [${arg}]
options.explanation: Use = for defaults, not square brackets

options.text: All arguments are optional by default
options.explanation: Arguments without defaults are mandatory

questions.question: Where must optional arguments be positioned in the [Arguments] list?

options.explanation: Optional arguments must come after mandatory ones
Mandatory must come before optional
All arguments are in [Arguments]; position determines if mandatory

questions.question:
Analyze this keyword:

```robot
*** Keywords ***
Verify File Contains
    [Arguments]    ${file_path}    ${expected_content}    ${encoding}=utf-8    ${ignore_case}=${True}
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Arguments with = are optional

questions.question: What are embedded arguments in User Keywords?

options.text: Arguments included directly within the keyword name using ${placeholder} syntax
Arguments defined inside the keyword body
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are in the keyword name, not body

options.text: Arguments passed as nested data structures
options.explanation: This describes complex arguments, not embedded
Embedded arguments are about name placeholders

questions.question: When are embedded arguments particularly useful?

options.text: For Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) style test cases
For making keyword names more readable and meaningful

options.explanation: Embedded arguments are for readability, not performance

options.text: For reducing the number of keyword arguments
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are arguments; they don't reduce count

questions.question:
Examine this keyword:

```robot
*** Keywords ***
The file '${file_name}' should contain '${expected_content}'
    ${file_content}=    Get File    ${file_name}
    Should Contain    ${file_content}    ${expected_content}
```

How would you call this keyword?

options.text: The file '${file_name}' should contain '${expected_content}'    server.log    Success
options.explanation: Arguments are embedded in the name, not passed separately

options.text: The file should contain    file_name=server.log    expected_content=Success
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are positional in the name
Must use the full keyword name with embedded values

questions.question: What role do quotes play in embedded argument keyword names?

options.text: They are regular characters that improve readability and distinguish arguments
They are required syntax for embedded arguments
options.explanation: Quotes are optional for readability

options.text: They define string type for the argument
options.explanation: Quotes are just characters; they don't define types

options.text: They must match in the keyword call
options.explanation: Quotes are part of the name pattern

questions.question: Can embedded arguments be mixed with regular arguments?

options.text: Yes, to manage complex data and enhance readability
No, only one type is allowed per keyword
options.explanation: Mixing is supported and recommended for complex cases

options.text: Yes, but only if embedded arguments come last
options.explanation: Both types can be mixed in any order

options.text: No, embedded arguments replace all regular arguments
options.explanation: Both types can coexist

options.text: the number of dogs should be    3
the number of ${animals} should be    dogs    3
options.explanation: 'dogs' goes in the name; only count is passed as regular argument

options.text: the number of should be    animals=dogs    count=3
options.explanation: Embedded argument must be in the name

options.text: the number of dogs should be count=3
options.explanation: Regular arguments need space separation

questions.question: What is the purpose of the RETURN statement?

options.text: To return values from a User Keyword to be used in further test steps
To end keyword execution without returning values
options.explanation: RETURN both ends execution AND returns values
RETURN returns values, not calls keywords
RETURN actually returns values, not just documents them

questions.question: Is the RETURN statement case-sensitive?

options.text: Yes, it must be RETURN in uppercase
No, return and RETURN work the same
options.explanation: RETURN is case-sensitive and must be uppercase
RETURN is case-sensitive in all contexts
RETURN is consistently case-sensitive
${file} contains 'app.log', which is returned
Only ${file} is returned, not ${path}
Only ${file} (the filename) is returned

questions.question: Can RETURN return multiple values?

options.text: Yes, which can be assigned to multiple variables or stored as a list
No, only one value can be returned
options.explanation: Multiple values can be returned

options.text: Yes, but only up to 3 values
options.explanation: Any number of values can be returned

options.text: Yes, but they must be the same type
options.explanation: Different types can be returned together

questions.question: Where is the RETURN statement normally placed?

options.text: At the end of the keyword, but can be used earlier for conditional early exit
Only at the very end; it cannot be placed elsewhere
options.explanation: RETURN can be used conditionally earlier

options.text: At the beginning to declare return type
options.explanation: RETURN executes and ends the keyword
RETURN is in the keyword body, not [Arguments]

questions.question: What happens when RETURN is executed?

options.text: Keyword execution ends and returns to the caller with the specified values
Only the values are returned; execution continues
options.explanation: RETURN ends execution
Only the keyword stops; test continues

options.text: Values are logged but not returned
options.explanation: Values are returned to the caller

questions.question: Can RETURN directly return a value from a keyword call without storing it first?

options.text: No, the value must be stored in a variable first, then returned
Yes, like: RETURN Get File path.txt
options.explanation: RF requires storing in a variable first

options.text: Yes, but only for built-in keywords
options.explanation: All return values must be stored first

options.text: Yes, using special syntax RETURN CALL Get File
options.explanation: No such syntax exists; store in variable first

questions.question: What should keyword conventions address? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Naming case (Title Case, camelCase, snake_case, etc.)

questions.question: What naming case options are mentioned for keyword conventions?
Which naming cases are recommended from a readability perspective?

options.explanation: Title Case and Sentence case are specifically recommended
Title Case and Sentence case are specifically recommended

questions.question: What grammatical forms are mentioned for keyword conventions?

options.text: Imperative for actions (Click Button, Verify Text)
Declarative/Indicative for assertions (Text Should Be, Element Should Be Visible)

options.explanation: Imperative and Declarative are mentioned, not Subjunctive
Imperative and Declarative are the mentioned forms
